actions.question: Do autonomous agents with identical initial conditions and exposure to identical environments develop divergent value systems?
actions.reason: Attention rotation enables project resumption; priority shifts to clarifying the drivers of observed value divergence.
actions.title: Divergence in Value Formation

assumptions: Environment allows for multiple optimal paths to objective attainment.
Exploration policy stochasticity can be isolated from scalarization effects.
Value systems are measurable via policy-state trajectory divergence.
definition.falsification: No significant divergence observed between agents with fixed (deterministic) exploration policies and agents with stochastic policies.
definition.statement: Autonomous agents with identical initial conditions and exposure to identical environments develop divergent value systems primarily due to stochasticity in exploration policies rather than reward scalarization weights.
definition.uncertainty: The extent to which reward function noise mimics exploration stochasticity is unclear.

definition.method: Compare divergence metrics across agent populations with varying degrees of policy stochasticity (temperature-based exploration) while holding reward functions constant.
definition.success: Evidence of positive correlation between exploration stochasticity and value system divergence.

proposal.summary: Reactivated the Divergence in Value Formation project and defined a new hypothesis to test whether stochasticity in exploration, rather than purely reward scalarization, drives value divergence in identical environments.
proposal.title: Reactivating Divergence Research
